advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'root is not a git work tree' from 'git exists but failed' in _git_listed, and surface the git failure (e.g. stderr warning or raise) instead of silently falling back to the whole-tree walk inside a .git-bearing root.
evidence: scripts/_repo_files.py:69-70: `listed = _git_listed(root)` / `relatives = _walked(root, patterns) if listed is None else listed` — a git failure is indistinguishable from 'outside a git work tree', both silently walk the whole tree

ABSENCE: no stderr diagnostic or marker is emitted when a repo that HAS .git fails `git ls-files`, so a gate pass after a silent fallback is indistinguishable from a true git-ignore-respecting pass — the fail-open litmus: the producer (git) never ran, yet the gate reports as if it did
scripts/_repo_files.py:51: `return [Path(os.fsdecode(entry)) for entry in completed.stdout.split(b"\0") if entry]` — an empty stdout yields `[]` with no distinction from a true empty listing
scripts/check_shellcheck.py:70-71: `if not files: return 0, ""` — an empty file set is an unconditional pass
advisory.finding: When `root/.git` exists but `git ls-files` exits non-zero (dubious-ownership in CI, a concurrent index lock, a corrupt repo) or raises OSError, `_git_listed` returns None and `files_named` silently falls back to the whole-tree rglob walk — the exact behavior that re-exhibits bug frouzy-downfallen-salamander (judging git-ignored venv/scratch files). There is no warning or signal that the git-ignore path was abandoned, so a transient git failure degrades the gate to the buggy pre-fix behavior invisibly.
merged_from: Inside a git work tree where `git ls-files` succeeds (returncode 0) with empty stdout, `files_named` returns an empty list and the gate passes green without scanning anything. An empty result from git is treated identically to a genuinely match-free tree, so a misconfiguration that makes git see no files (e.g. `root` is not the worktree top but a `.git` gitdir file resolves an unexpected tree) produces a vacuous pass rather than a diagnosable failure.
scenarios: CI checkout owned by a different uid triggers git 'detected dubious ownership', ls-files exits 128, gate silently walks the tree and relints an ignored venv's activate.sh (the original bug) or, conversely, flakily passes/fails depending on environment
A concurrent git operation holds the index lock during make lint

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a files_named() test that commits a matching file, deletes it from the worktree, and asserts it is excluded from the returned list.
evidence: scripts/_repo_files.py:64-66 docstring: 'A path is dropped when any of its repo-relative parts is in ``excluded_dirs``, or when it is not a file (a matching directory, or a tracked file deleted from the work tree).'

Named violating input: `a/tracked.sh` added+committed to git, then removed from the worktree (`rm a/tracked.sh` without `git rm`); `git ls-files --cached` still lists `a/tracked.sh`, so files_named() must drop it via is_file() — ABSENCE: no test in test_uv_pin_guard.py (test_files_named_*) or the gate tests creates-then-deletes a tracked match.
advisory.finding: files_named()'s is_file() guard — which the module docstring calls out as handling 'a tracked file deleted from the work tree' — is untested. Inside git, `git ls-files --cached` lists a tracked file even after it is removed from the working tree; without the is_file() filter the gates would attempt to read a nonexistent path. No test plants a tracked *.sh/*.tf/Dockerfile and deletes it from the worktree to prove files_named() drops the stale entry.
scenarios: A contributor deletes a tracked shell script from the worktree without committing; a gate that lost the is_file() guard would crash trying to read it.
A behavior-preserving refactor of _git_listed that forgets the is_file() filter would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_uv_pin_guard.py add a test: create and `git add`+`init` a tracked `a/tracked.sh`, then `(tmp_path / 'a' / 'tracked.sh').unlink()`, and assert `files_named(tmp_path, ('*.sh',), frozenset())` does not contain that path.
